common_assumptions: Current file state matches last-read version without re-reading between edits
Compilation or type-check success implies behavioral correctness
PATH tools (node, npm, tsc, pm2, rg) are available at expected versions
Prior session context from WAL or checkpoints accurately reflects current disk state
Single-file edits will resolve bugs that span multiple files or runtime interactions
strength_patterns: Systematic multi-command diagnostic sequencing before attempting fixes, narrowing problem space methodically
Post-change verification via type checks, server health probes, and log inspection
Thorough file exploration and reading for context before editing in unfamiliar areas
weakness_patterns: Fixation loops on single files with incremental edits without stepping back to verify system-level behavior — f3ddfd2f ran 30+ statusline.sh read/write cycles, fc4190a7 made 17+ edits to +layout.svelte
Substituting compile or collect passes (tsc --noEmit, npx tsc) for runtime exercise and reporting success without observing actual behavior
Low exploration breadth — chains are predominantly linear sequential tool calls with minimal branching; alternative approaches are rarely generated and compared before committing to a path
